title: KestrelCare Trip Interruption: Trip Days, Release Date and Receipt Period
content:
## The decision and the repair order

A KestrelCare Vehicle Service Contracts trip interruption reimbursement is figured on the plan's most recent approved decision: its repair order, failure date, decision date, vehicle system, estimate and deductible, together with the claim payments posted on that repair order.

## Trip days and amount

The trip days are the calendar days from the failure date on the decision to the day the vehicle is released, which is the date of the latest claim payment posted on the repair order, the facility releasing the vehicle when it is paid, or the decision date where no claim payment has posted. The trip days are capped at the plan's trip interruption maximum days, and the reimbursement is the capped trip days times the plan's trip interruption per-day amount, rounded to the cent. A count of trip days is never below zero.

| Claim payments posted on the repair order | Day the vehicle is released |
|---|---|
| one or more | the date of the latest of them |
| none | the decision date |

## Receipts and once per repair order

Trip interruption receipts are accepted within the plan's benefit receipt submission days counted in calendar days from the day the vehicle is released, and trip interruption is reimbursed once per repair order. A claim outside that period, or on a repair order already carrying a trip interruption reimbursement entry, is reimbursed nothing.

## Worked figures (hypothetical plan: maximum 3 days, 100.00 per day, receipts within 30 days)

Failure date 12 May; decision 13 May; claim payments posted on the repair order on 14 May and 17 May. The vehicle is released on 17 May, giving 5 trip days, capped at 3: the reimbursement is 300.00. Receipts are accepted through 16 June, the thirtieth day after the release.

Had no claim payment posted, the release day would be the decision date, 13 May, giving 1 trip day and 100.00.
